This game is so good. I was so moved by the ending even though I've already played the original game and I knew what was going to happen. The story was very well written and told that I did not feel it was spoiled at all.

Pros
Great Combat: The fighting mechanics are engaging and genuinely fun to play. Much better than Remake imo.

Strong Story/Characters: The narrative is compelling so far, and the character writing keeps you invested.

Addictive Mini game: The card game is a highlight and a standout feature.

Cons
Artificial Padding: It feels like the developers were forced to stretch playtime by adding unnecessary seconds to every interaction (like staring at a lever for 5 seconds before pulling it).

Tedious Traversal: Level design often feels illogical, forcing you to climb up and down ladders just to cross simple distances.

Clunky Movement: Even the chocobos feel heavy and cumbersome, constantly slowing down over small terrain imperfections. The scent mechanic is annoying after a while too.

Mini games: Most of them are tedious like forced stealth sections that make you take the longest paths (second chocobo wrangle) 

Pacing Issues: The open world elements are frustratingly slow, dragging down an otherwise excellent experience. I pray they do not do this style of game again this was the worst open world game I have played in a while I don't think they know what makes them fun.

As an FF7 OG fan, much like many others here, I have thoroughly enjoyed the journey so far. I literally cannot describe or don't possess the right adjectives to express how I feel about this game. It's fun, exciting, memorable, full of catchy music, amusing characters (except Chadley), and every location is an absolutely jaw-dropper, every.single.time. Absolutely cannot WAIT for the final part of the trilogy and while it may leave us empty, BRING IT ON!

The sheer amount of awful quality and boring side quests is baffling, I'm struggling to think of A SINGLE fun side quest.
Some of the encounters leave barely any wiggle room when several enemies that cover each other's weaknesses, for example Alexander + Odin BS fight.
AND LASTLY the ending, killing THE ONE SINGULAR decent character is the most not fun and unsatisfying way to end this horrid experience. I feel like I wasted over 100 hours.

Compared to the first of the FF7 Remakes, I did not enjoy Rebirth as much. The player is incentivized to explore the large open world environments to completion, but these environments have very, very repetitive gameplay elements. Rebirth would have been a better game if they stayed to closed environments like the first game. Also the story didn't really catch me as hard as the first game. Some moments in the first game genuinely made me cry, no parts of Rebirth have made me emotional.

I loved the Remake part 1. There were some side quests but there were only a few each chapter so i finished most of them. The game felt magical and fresh and it wasn's actually that long.
Then there is this game.
Where they try to make it as hard as they possibly can to stray you from the main story, so much, that you almost forget it exists.
The game is pretty. The world that is not related to the main game is empty. If you loved wasting your time in Horizon Zero Dawn or Ghost of Tsushima and pranced doing same quests over and over then this is a game for you. Of course you can skip so much of that fluff. But even then, the game tries to push you into at least a little bit of it, like the slog that chocobo hunting mini games are.
It's a game designed to make you lose your precious life as much as they can. And as seen by the reviews, many players absolutely love that.
I hated that. I have enough boring chores in real lilfe to do to play Cait Sith and trying to throw some boxes for 2 hours.
Then you check the original game and remember that those stories only take max several hours. And it explains everything.
This is the best game. It has something for everyone. most of the optional stuff is in fact optional. dont let others fool you. THis game is beautiful and combat is top tier.

The cutscenes are in depth, emotional, and some of them are even funny. I liked Barret and Yuffie's interaction lmao.

Once again, just like Crisis Core, I couldn't get over the ending even five months after I finished it. I really miss it. I miss the game, the characters, and the story.

I also liked how I was able to control each character during the battle, it felt cool when I could just switch up and beat the enemy up lol.

While it *is* definitely bloated to the point that it is hard to recognize the actual story in this game (which is still good), giving this a thumbs down is absurd, given how good the gameplay, presentation, optimization and main story are. Still, painful to see that they could have just postponed all the side-content to the end of the game, gotten rid of all the completion lists during the main story, and everyone (including me) would say this is the perfect remake. It's just hard to get into the "we're being followed by Shinra and we're hunting this mysterious dude"-vibe, if at *every* *single* *corner*, you have hours worth of happy-hippo-side-content.

I am about halfway through the main story while doing all of the sidequests. I've noticed they've made several fixes to the lighting system compared the its original release, and it really helps in staying in the world. 

If you like RPGs, this is one of the all-time greats.

Another buggy port from Square Enix. They released this knowing that even top of the line AMD GPUs were barely supported, and would frequently crash. No AMD FrameGen support, regular crashes to desktop. Very disappointing.

From AMD's site: "Intermittent system or application crash may be observed while playing FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH for long periods of time." --- I guess "long periods" means 30 minutes max. No way Square was unaware of this issue.

The continuation from remake, all the system from the first game are expended and polished.
The battle system is both engaging and strategic.
The world is huge and diverse.
The cast is fun and endearing.
The main plot take a back step and the focus is more on character development and world building compared to remake.
There is a completely new "exploration" gameplay that was absent in remake.

Love the characters, love the combat, love the visuals of the world, & like that there are a variety of minigames that can be a nice distraction from the combat or the main story.

Lukewarm towards the ending of the story & the open world activities. For anyone who plans to play it, I recommend not getting caught up with all of the side activities. None of the rewards from the side activities are necessary & missing out on them isn't going to hinder you from finishing the main story. You will ruin the pacing of the story if try to complete all of them as soon as they become available.

Disliked the stutters in a few of the big towns. Square needs to push out more updates to address the stutters & overall high VRAM & GPU demand of the game. Thankfully, I didn't encounter the stutters during combat but the vibe of exploring some of the towns is ruined by the stutters.

Despite the flaws, it's still among my favorites of all time.

I have a lot to say about this game, but I'll keep it to two points.

- Horrible writing...if you're going to change a perfect story, at least make sure it's well written.
- WAY too much filler. The game is 80% fetch quests and mini games. I'm not exaggerating. 20% ffvii, 80% Mario Party.

I enjoyed remake and I hope the 3rd game is better.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (78%): players love the story and characters, and the combat wins praise too.
The most common complaint is boring, tedious quests, with the side content and combat also drawing criticism.

details.text: Recent reviews have slipped a little, with performance complaints edging up while story complaints ease.
Players who reviewed with little time in the game are far less positive, at 59%, than long-time players, at 81%.
